inspected_published_library_suppliers.inspected_contract: A random element is a measurable map into the target measurable space; real random variables use the Borel sigma-algebra.
The law is the pushforward measure, P_X(B)=P(X^{-1}(B)).
Nonnegative measurable variables have extended nonnegative expectation; integrable variables have finite real/complex expectation.
Independence is independence of the generated event sigma-algebras.
A finite tuple of independent random elements has the product joint law on the finite product sigma-algebra.
The actual definition is for set families on a finite ground set [n], not a general-domain hypothesis class.
For a family on [n] with VC dimension at most d, |F| <= sum_{i=0}^d binom(n,i); proof is finite combinatorial down-shifting.
For real L2 input and a sub-sigma-algebra, conditional expectation is the unique almost-sure L2 minimizer; the item assumes AC.
An RCD exists for a standard-Borel target and arbitrary conditioning sub-sigma-algebra; the item assumes AC.
Tonelli applies to nonnegative product-measurable functions on sigma-finite product measure spaces.
Fubini applies to L1 functions on sigma-finite product spaces; exceptional sections are handled a.e.
The actual theorem assumes AC, sigma-finite positive and signed measures with a common finite exhaustion, and absolute continuity; finite probability measures meet finiteness conditions.
Defines N_d(m,Sigma) for symmetric PSD Sigma, permits singular covariance, and assumes AC in its construction.
